claims.text: When humans experience stress, the body activates the same physiological responses as an animal's body.
Humans do not resolve psychological conflict through fighting or fleeing.
Prolonged activation of the stress response causes or intensifies a range of physical and mental afflictions over time.

evidence.description: When we worry or experience stress, our body turns on the same physiological responses that an animal's does.
Humans do not resolve conflict in the same way as animals—through fighting or fleeing.
Prolonged stress causes or intensifies a range of physical and mental afflictions, including depression, ulcers, colitis, heart disease, and more.
